AI Use Log

This log records substantive uses of AI that influenced my portfolio, as required by the portfolio guidelines. Minor interactions (for example, single syntax questions) are not logged. I remain responsible for checking and understanding all AI-assisted material, and all analysis results were produced by running the code myself in R.

Project 2: Predicting drought in the Western Cape

Date Tool used What I asked it to help with Link What I checked or changed myself
2026-10-29 Claude (Cowork) Reviewing Project 2 against the portfolio guidelines and rubric, using my rendered HTML output. It identified text that contradicted the tables, unfinished placeholder text, a model chosen using the test set, a cross-correlation driven by seasonality, a missing seasonal MA candidate for SST, and a bias from averaging whichever buoys reported each day. Conversation I checked each issue against my rendered tables and figures before accepting it.
2026-10-29 Claude (Cowork) Revising the analysis code: a justified set of seven candidate models, rolling-origin cross-validation for model selection, an ETS(A,N,A) comparison, a composition-adjusted daily SST mean, Ljung-Box tests, and saving key results so the summary page updates automatically. Conversation Claude could not run R, so I rendered the code myself, reported errors back (a YAML caption error) and checked every table and figure. I replaced Claude’s hand-coded prewhitening filter with TSA::prewhiten(), since prewhitening was not covered in lectures and a package function with an explanation was more appropriate.
2026-10-29 Claude (Cowork) Explaining concepts I had not used before: CRPS, the Ljung-Box \(Q\) statistic, prewhitening, rolling-origin cross-validation and the buoy composition adjustment (including writing it as an equation). Conversation I checked the explanations against Hyndman & Athanasopoulos (2021) and Cryer & Chan (2008), and asked for simpler explanations until I could explain each one in my own words.
2026-10-29 Claude (Cowork) Rewording draft paragraphs and replacing conditional inline R text with sentences based on my final rendered results. Conversation I edited the wording and corrected the interpretation where I disagreed. I pointed out that the SST trend was not more stable than the dam trend (it tracks El Niño and La Niña events), that the positive lag-6 correlation contradicts the hypothesised negative relationship, and that the unit root tests choose the differencing while the ACF and PACF choose the AR and MA orders.
2026-10-29 Claude (Cowork) Suggesting references for the methods and software used (Hyndman & Athanasopoulos; Cryer & Chan; the fable, feasts and TSA packages). Conversation Claude said that some reference details were from memory and that its first prewhitening citation was wrong. I checked the package references with citation() in R and the textbook chapter numbers against the books.

Project 3: Predicting the volatility of JSE All Share Index returns

Date Tool used What I asked it to help with Link What I checked or changed myself
2026-10-08 Claude (Cowork) Reviewing my first version of Project 3 against the course ARCH and GARCH guide. It found that the sector extension had failed fits (degrees of freedom at the lower bound and identical half-lives for every sector), that EGARCH was difficult to interpret, and that some template text contradicted my diagnostic results. It suggested a simplified structure following the guide’s ten-step workflow. Conversation [Add what you checked or changed yourself.]
2026-10-29 Claude (Cowork) Reviewing Project 3 against the portfolio guidelines and rubric, using my rendered HTML output. It identified broken inline R code, typos, a broken table reference, an incorrect long-run volatility in the summary, a methods paragraph that did not match the analysis, and that the test period was much calmer than the training period. Conversation I checked each issue against my rendered tables and figures before accepting it.
2026-10-29 Claude (Cowork) Checking whether the Diebold–Mariano test was covered in the course notes, and adding Diebold–Mariano tests and Value-at-Risk backtests (Kupiec and Christoffersen) to the analysis. Conversation Claude confirmed that these tests are not in the course notes, slides or ARCH and GARCH guide. I asked for them to be implemented with forecast::dm.test() and rugarch::VaRTest() instead of from first principles, and asked for the code to be simplified so that it did not generate the interpretation text. Claude could not run R, so I rendered the code myself and wrote the interpretations from my rendered tables.
2026-10-29 Claude (Cowork) Rewording and condensing draft paragraphs (mean model selection, diagnostics, Diebold–Mariano and VaR results), and explaining why the models are evaluated on a test set. Conversation I edited the wording and wrote the results into the interpretations myself. Claude then checked the summary page against my results and corrected contradictions, for example the limitations paragraph that said the GARCH ranking was uncertain after the Diebold–Mariano tests showed significant differences.
2026-10-29 Claude (Cowork) Suggesting references for the methods and software used (Patton, 2011; Diebold & Mariano, 1995; Kupiec, 1995; Christoffersen, 1998; Hyndman & Khandakar, 2008). Conversation [Add how you checked the references, e.g. against the DOIs and citation() in R.]
